clue.text: One thing a bachelor cannot immediately become

definitions.text: One thing a bachelor cannot immediately become

parts.words: One thing a bachelor cannot immediately become
parts.note: a single man must marry once before he can take a second spouse unlawfully, so he cannot reach that state straight away

explanation.definitionFit: Someone with two spouses at once has already had to marry once, which an unmarried man has not.

clue.text: Game for a dance at Head-quarters ?

parts.note: headquarters of an operation is its base
a ball is a formal dance

explanation.surface: Whether a dance held at headquarters is something people are up for.
explanation.definitionFit: The American bat-and-ball sport is a game.

clue.text: Attained a certain degree of success

definitions.text: Attained a certain degree of success

parts.words: Attained a certain degree of success
parts.note: degree here is a university qualification: someone who earned one finished their studies successfully

explanation.surface: Achieved some measure of success.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A certain degree' seems to mean 'to some extent'; it is an academic degree.
explanation.definitionFit: Completing a course and receiving a university award is earning a degree.

clue.text: They acquire tone in Kent

parts.note: adding the word tone to young women servants makes the name of the county town of Kent

explanation.surface: People who gain refinement in a southern English county.
explanation.walkthrough: Maidstone is the county town of Kent, a county in south-east England; add TONE to the answer to make it.
explanation.definitionFit: Young female servants, which with the word tone added form a Kentish town name.

clue.text: Members of the barber's shop quartette ?

definitions.text: Members of the barber's shop quartette ?

parts.words: Members of the barber's shop quartette
parts.note: barbershop is a style of close-harmony unaccompanied vocal music, so the quartet is of vocalists, not hairdressers

explanation.surface: The four people who work in a barber's shop.
explanation.walkthrough: A barbershop quartet is a four-voice close-harmony group, not barbers.
explanation.definitionFit: Members of a vocal group are vocalists.

clue.text: Result of aiming high?

explanation.definitionFit: An outcome or conclusion is the final result; read literally, a shot fired upward is one aimed high.

clue.text: Tool for a writer — or one engaged in swan-upping ?

explanation.walkthrough: Swan-upping is the annual English ceremony of catching and marking swans on the Thames; a female swan is a pen, so one holding swans holds pens.
explanation.definitionFit: A handle into which a nib fits is a writing implement; someone grasping female swans at the swan census is literally gripping pens.

clue.text: He has a bit, but not to eat

definitions.text: He has a bit, but not to eat

parts.words: He has a bit, but not to eat
parts.note: a bit is the metal mouthpiece of a bridle, not a morsel of food, though it sits in the animal's mouth

explanation.surface: Someone holding a morsel he does not intend to eat.
explanation.definitionFit: A ridden animal wears a bridle whose metal mouthpiece is called a bit.

clue.text: Diplomatic attempt to take food in

definitions.note: the adjective stands for a diplomatic agreement, a noun

indicators.note: in places the food-taking piece inside the attempt

parts.note: an attempt is a try
to take food is to eat

explanation.surface: A diplomat tries to get some food down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Diplomatic' acts as shorthand for a diplomatic agreement.
explanation.definitionFit: A formal agreement between states is the business of diplomacy.

clue.text: Held to be self-evident by independent Americans

definitions.text: Held to be self-evident by independent Americans

parts.words: Held to be self-evident by independent Americans
parts.note: the Declaration of Independence opens its second sentence 'We hold these ... to be self-evident'

explanation.surface: Things free-thinking Americans take for granted.
explanation.walkthrough: The US Declaration of Independence says 'We hold these truths to be self-evident'; 'independent' points to that document.
explanation.definitionFit: Facts or principles accepted as certain, as in the famous American declaration.

clue.text: He is of material assistance to the writer

definitions.text: He is of material assistance to the writer

parts.words: He is of material assistance to the writer
parts.note: material here means writing materials, paper, envelopes and ink sold by a shopkeeper, not material help

explanation.surface: Someone gives a writer practical support.
explanation.definitionFit: A shopkeeper selling paper and pens supplies the materials a writer uses.

clue.text: Its loss may cause panic

parts.note: the idiom of losing one's courage or composure under strain describes someone who then panics

explanation.surface: Something whose disappearance sets off alarm.
explanation.definitionFit: Courage or steadiness under pressure, which once lost leaves a person panicking.

clue.text: Sadness of a cavalry regiment

explanation.definitionFit: Melancholy is often called by this colour name; the Royal Horse Guards cavalry regiment was nicknamed after its uniform colour.

clue.text: Don't ask him to look into things

definitions.text: Don't ask him to look into things

parts.words: Don't ask him to look into things
parts.note: an outgoing person turns attention outward rather than inward, so looking into things, introspection, is not his habit

explanation.surface: Advice not to give someone an investigation to run.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Look into things' seems to mean investigate; it means look inward, the opposite of this personality type.
explanation.definitionFit: An outgoing, sociable person is directed outward, unlike the introspective type.

clue.text: They secure doors of ramshackle chalets

indicators.note: ramshackle means tumbledown and disordered, so the letters of the following word are thrown into a new order

explanation.surface: Fastenings keep the doors shut on some rickety holiday huts.
explanation.definitionFit: Simple bar fastenings are what hold doors and gates closed.

clue.text: Ambitious pilot ?

parts.note: an ambitious person aims at the top, and a pilot literally flies at altitude

explanation.surface: An aviator with big ambitions.
explanation.definitionFit: A person on course for great success, read literally as an aviator at altitude.

clue.text: Where to find old buffers and slow-coaches ?

definitions.text: Where to find old buffers and slow-coaches ?

parts.words: Where to find old buffers and slow-coaches
parts.note: buffers are the sprung stops on railway wagons and slow coaches are railway carriages; both sit in a short side track off the main line

explanation.surface: A place where elderly fogeys and dawdlers gather.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Old buffers' and 'slow-coaches' look like dull people; they are railway hardware parked off the main line.
explanation.definitionFit: A short railway track beside the main line where wagons and coaches are parked.

clue.text: Feeling somewhat uneasy when abroad?

parts.note: the idiom for feeling ill at ease also literally describes someone who is away from their own house, as a traveller abroad is

explanation.surface: A traveller's mild discomfort overseas.
explanation.definitionFit: Being ill at ease is the idiom; a person abroad is literally away from their own house.

clue.text: They are put up in the closing act

definitions.text: They are put up in the closing act

parts.words: They are put up in the closing act
parts.note: the closing act is a shopkeeper shutting up for the night, when boards are put up over the windows

explanation.surface: Scenery erected for the last act of a play.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Closing act' suggests a play's finale; it is shutting the shop.
explanation.definitionFit: Window boards or panels fitted when closing a shop or house.

clue.text: Sayings of the Christian Era?

parts.note: AD, anno domini, is how years of the Christian calendar are marked
an era is a long period, as are ages

explanation.surface: Proverbs from the time of the early church.
explanation.definitionFit: Old proverbs or maxims are traditional sayings.

clue.text: Who's dispatched to the railway? A guard, naturally

parts.note: to dispatch is to send off, so dispatched means sent

explanation.surface: A railway guard being sent off to work.
explanation.definitionFit: A soldier standing watch at a post is a guard.

clue.text: Wound that is no handicap

explanation.walkthrough: In golf a player with no handicap is called a 'scratch' player.
explanation.definitionFit: A minor cut is a light wound; a golfer playing off zero handicap is a scratch golfer.

clue.text: For Hamlet it was the last word

definitions.text: For Hamlet it was the last word

parts.words: For Hamlet it was the last word
parts.note: the prince's dying line in Shakespeare's play is 'The rest is ...', so the final word he speaks ends the speech

explanation.surface: The final say belonged to the Danish prince.
explanation.walkthrough: Hamlet's last words are 'The rest is silence.'
explanation.definitionFit: Hamlet's dying line ends with this word for quiet.

clue.text: American processing of fuel that's serviceable

parts.note: US is short for American, as in US forces

indicators.note: processing works raw material over, so the letters of the next word are refashioned

explanation.surface: A US method of refining fuel that works well.
explanation.walkthrough: 'processing of' rearranges the letters of 'fuel' into EFUL.
explanation.definitionFit: Something serviceable is practical and of use.

clue.text: One of two matches is not quite conclusive

explanation.definitionFit: A tournament has two penultimate-round games before the final; read as 'half final' it is not quite the deciding game.

clue.text: Sign when taking away

explanation.definitionFit: The arithmetic symbol for subtraction is a sign; as a preposition it means less or without.

clue.text: Met to compose Church music

indicators.note: to compose is to put together or arrange, so the letters of the two words before it are rearranged

explanation.surface: Gathering together to write music for a service.
explanation.definitionFit: A short choral piece sung in church services is a sacred anthem of this kind.

clue.text: With a corn, I am in a state of bewilderment

indicators.note: I am in says the letter I sits inside the next piece

parts.note: to be in a maze is to be bewildered

explanation.surface: Someone with a sore foot is confused.
explanation.walkthrough: 'With a corn' suggests a sore toe; corn is the grain.
explanation.definitionFit: In American usage corn is the cereal crop also called Indian corn.

clue.text: Mouldy sorts of amusement a soldier goes after

indicators.note: goes after means the soldier piece is placed following the amusement piece

parts.note: amusement means enjoyment, fun
GI is an American enlisted soldier

explanation.surface: A soldier in pursuit of entertainment of a stale, musty kind.
explanation.definitionFit: Moulds and mildews belong to the kingdom of mushrooms and toadstools.

clue.text: Wild fellow has the makings of a top-liner

indicators.note: having the makings of something means holding the raw materials for it, so the letters of the phrase are rebuilt into a new word

explanation.surface: A tearaway who could become a headline star.
explanation.walkthrough: 'has the makings of' rearranges the letters of 'a top-liner'. A rantipole is an old word for a wild, rakish person.
explanation.definitionFit: An archaic term for a reckless, unruly person.

clue.text: Is worsted appropriate wear for them ?

definitions.text: Is worsted appropriate wear for them ?

parts.words: Is worsted appropriate wear for them
parts.note: worsted is a woollen cloth, but to be worsted is to be beaten, which suits people who fail to win

explanation.surface: A question of whether a wool fabric suits certain people.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Worsted' looks like the cloth; it is the past participle of 'worst', to defeat.
explanation.definitionFit: Those beaten in a contest are the defeated side.

clue.text: Hare-brained youngsters

parts.note: hare-brained normally means reckless, but here it means young creatures with a hare's brain, that is, baby hares

explanation.surface: Reckless young people.
explanation.definitionFit: Young hares in their first year are given this special name.
